reasons: As an ad photograph the stud is not the hero, and this is what holds the score under the run bar. At true scale it spans 235 x 110 px (alpha x 347-581, y 1652-1761). That is 22% of the width of its 1080 px 4:5 framing [40,600,1120,1950] and about 1.8% of the frame area, beside four loose sugared sweets of about 250-290 px and a heaped glass bowl that take the eye first. At 390 px wide it is about 85 x 40 px and reads as a small jewel lying by the sweets. Its only rhyme with the candy is colour (purple, pink and yellow against lilac, pink and lemon jellies), so 'almost edible' does not land in one second. The sugar's sparkle also out-shines it: it is the sharpest thing in the frame, not the brightest.

Shadow vector and softness: shx=50, shy=20 throws the top edge's shadow 22 degrees below horizontal from the contact point (455,1761). The measured shadow spans x 383-611, y 1732-1785, its centroid only (+29,+7) px from the contact, so it reads as a soft sideways smear. The sweets' own sun is about 37-38 degrees up and 14-20 degrees left of the camera axis, behind the set: about (0.43,0.66) px of offset per px of height, with the camera about 28 degrees up. Under that sun, the top edge of a 10 mm face leaning back to 63 degrees (89 px of rise, less 24 px for its 4.5 mm lean) should land at about (+38,+35), or 43 degrees. That matches the sweets, whose shadows run 52-61 degrees from their own contacts. blur 5.0 at the far edge (about 13 px from 10% to 90%) is roughly twice what a throw of 10 mm or less should get, given the sweets' 16-24 px at 30-36 mm.

Light on the face: the stud keeps the macro's soft frontal light. Under that back-left sun, a face leaning back to 63 degrees faces away from the sun (normal-to-sun dot product about -0.4), so it would sit in its own shade, with sun only on the pearls' tops and the claws' rims. Here the pearls and metal are evenly lit grey-white (median RGB 226,209,204). The rim (0.45) and grad (0.06) help, but at full size the stud reads as a studio cut-out. The yellow stone's glow (0.6) leaves a smooth orange smudge directly under it at x 440-470, y 1758-1770, which reads as a reflection on a glossy floor.
notes: Fidelity holds: the piece is the listing macro listing-5.jpg. The plate reproduces exactly from comp_cluster.py's defaults (maximum difference 0). Inside the stud (8,533 core px) its high-pass structure correlates 0.993 with the scaled listing, rotated 1.5 degrees. The only changes are the grade (tint 1.0/0.965/0.935, lift 34/26/24, gain 0.96, grad 0.06), a 0.45 rim on the upper-left edges, and grain 1.8. The metal reads white (median RGB 232,218,214, R/B 1.075), warmed toward the blush set.

Stone order matches the listing text and the macro. Left to right: purple princess (x 355-400), pink baguette (395-432), yellow emerald-cut at the centre and the largest (432-478), purple princess (480-535), pink baguette (525-570). There are 8 pearls, at about (361,1663) at the left tip, (404,1681) in the upper gap, (385,1719) under the first purple, (425,1744) under the pink, (489,1751) at the yellow's lower right, (513,1693) above the second purple, (536,1736) under the second purple and pink, and (571,1690) at the right tip. That is the brand's own macro, so it is not a plate fault. The listing text says six pearls: an open question for the founder. The plate is fine as long as no copy states a count.

Scale is true. Circle fits put the pink sweet beside the stud at 277.8 px and the right purple at 290.2. The stud is 0.85 of the pink sweet's width, about 0.81 of a sweet at its own depth (it stands about 125 px nearer the camera, where sweets draw about 4% larger). With 2.5 cm sweets it is about 20.3 mm (+1% against 20 mm); with 2.0 cm sweets, 16.2 mm (-19%); at the script's 2.2 cm, 17.8 mm. The yellow emerald-cut is 43 x 65 px, about 3.8 x 5.7 mm at that depth's 11.5 px/mm. This agrees with the Prism plate, whose 5 mm stones put these sweets at about 2.5 cm.

Contact and physics hold. The stud stands on its lowest claw at (455,1761) with contact darkening (ao 0.6). Its arc ends are raised (the first purple's bottom at about y 1719, the second pink's at about 1730-1740), and those raised ends correctly cast detached shadows, as an arc resting on its lowest point should. No double shadow: none of its shadow falls on ground already shaded (0 px). The right end (x 527-579) sits in front of the pink sweet's shadow on screen but is sunlit in 3-D (its shadow-test point lands at about (603,1789), outside the sweet's shadow), so full brightness there is right. Nothing overlaps the stud, so the occlusion is right. The deepest shadow, 0.75/0.60/0.57 of lit, is a little lighter than the sweets' 0.69/0.55/0.50, which is fair for stones that pass light.

Cut-out edges are clean (masks/cluster-listing-5.png). There is no plinth fringe even where the right end meets the dark sweet shadow (x 560-585, y 1670-1730), and the 1.2 px feather matches the scene's edges. The sharpness index is 0.74 against the sweets' 0.50-0.72, within range. Grain is 1.8 against the paper's about 2.5.

Phone size (the 4:5 framing at 390 px): a viewer would not suspect a composite; the stud reads as a real jewel lying in the sun by the sweets. At full size the giveaways are the soft sideways shadow (x 383-611, y 1732-1785), unlike the sweets' crisp diagonal shadows, and the evenly lit pearls.

Score 8.0, under the 8.5 run bar for composition, not realism. The palette, the hard sun and the calm upper left are on brand, and the stud is crisp and true to size. But it is too small, and too unlike a sweet, for the pun to read in the thumbnail. As an ad it would also carry the pre-order cap (9.5).
